definition: Admonish means to scold someone for a fault in a firm but measured way.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word admonish. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know admonish should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The lifeguard admonished the boys for running on the wet tiles — once, quietly, and with the whistle still around her neck.
A reminder carries no blame at all — milder than admonish, which says plainly that a line was crossed.
Scold goes further than admonish: there is open anger in a scolding, where admonish stays level and measured.

To caution is to warn someone about a danger or misstep before it happens, with no blame attached. A reminder can only re-tell what someone already knows; a caution can be brand-new information. And where caution looks forward, admonish looks back — it corrects, firmly but calmly, a line already crossed.

A reprimand is a formal, on-the-record scolding — the kind that ends up in a personnel file, and it is harsher than admonish. To admonish is milder and usually private: firm words meant to fix conduct, not to punish it. A manager admonishes you in the hallway; a board reprimands you in writing.
